transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this course-review meeting for the proposed Community Data and Public Life course, INT-200. Before I can sign off on the proposal, I need to hear from each of you on any requirements or corrections within your area of responsibility. Let's start with the faculty sponsor — could you please present your report on the pilot? And I'll need the completed pilot report formally placed into the meeting record, not just a verbal summary. Registrar and library representative, please be ready to follow with your respective reports.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Nair. I ran a pilot of INT-200 this term and completed the pilot report yesterday. The pilot findings require two key corrections to the proposal: first, students must complete exactly 20 hours of supervised community fieldwork; and second, a faculty-reviewed portfolio is required instead of a final examination. The proposal file currently still contains the earlier draft, so those updates need to be reflected. I am now formally placing the completed pilot report into the meeting record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical correction regarding the course code and contact hours. The confirmed transfer-articulation record I received from the partner college yesterday assigns this course the code INT-205 — not INT-200 as currently proposed — and requires exactly 45 instructional contact hours for the three-credit equivalency. The proposal currently lists INT-200 and 30 contact hours, both of which conflict with the articulation record. I have not yet entered these changes into the catalog workflow, but they must be reflected before approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical correction regarding the course materials. I confirmed the publisher license terms this week: the license for the course case materials permits access only to enrolled students through the college's password-protected e-reserve system and explicitly prohibits posting the materials on a public website. However, the proposal currently states that learning materials will be posted on the public course website. This must be corrected before approval — the proposal should reflect that materials will be made available through the e-reserve system instead.
transcript.speaker: A4
